# zeroword_api_key (Resource)

A Management API key. Keys cannot be edited: every change revokes the key and issues a new one. The provider's own key must hold every scope granted here (and `api_keys:write`). A key revoked or expired outside Terraform is issued again on the next apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "zeroword_api_key" "deletion_job" {
  workspace_id   = data.zeroword_workspace.this.id
  environment_id = zeroword_environment.staging.id
  name           = "account deletion job"
  scopes         = ["users:read", "users:delete"]
}

output "deletion_job_api_key" {
  value     = zeroword_api_key.deletion_job.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name (1-200 characters).
- `scopes` (Set of String) Granted scopes, e.g. `users:read`.
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace ID (`wsp_...`). Must be the provider key's Workspace.

### Optional

- `environment_id` (String) Pin the key to this Environment. Omit for a Workspace-scoped key.
- `expires_at` (String) Expiry as RFC 3339 timestamp. Omit for a key without expiry.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) API key ID (`mky_...`).
- `prefix` (String) Non-secret display prefix of the key.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The key (`sk_live_...`). Zeroword returns it only at creation, so it is null after import. Stored in state; protect the state backend.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The secret is not returned after creation, so it is null after import.
terraform import zeroword_api_key.deletion_job mky_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```
